overview: The City Council commemorated the life of long-time political follower Leonard Glenn Gliona and approved a $1.69 million appropriation for a new fire ladder truck. The Council also advanced a new vacant building ordinance and accepted a state grant for archaeological work at a redevelopment site in Medford Square.

items.title: Resolution to Commemorate Leonard Glenn Gliona
items.summary: Approved a resolution offering condolences and honoring the life of Lenny Gliona, a veteran and dedicated local political mentor. The Council held a moment of silence following remarks from every councilor and former Councilor Nicole Morell.

items.title: Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved meeting records from April 28, 2026, and committee reports regarding Community Development Block Grants and the fiscal 2027 budget.

items.title: CDBG Action Plan for Fiscal 2027 Hearing
items.summary: Approved the annual action plan for $1,433,520 in federal block grant funds after a public hearing and presentation by Grants Manager Laurel Siegel.

items.title: Appointments and Event Licenses
items.summary: Approved the appointment of Roberta Cameron to the Historic District Commission and authorized food truck permits for a youth softball tournament at Tufts Park.

items.title: Fire Department Capital Improvement Appropriations
items.summary: Approved $2,111,401.84 from the Capital Stabilization Fund for a new ladder truck, equipment for upcoming pumpers, and department administrative vehicles. Fire Chief Todd Evans explained that rising costs and four-year lead times necessitated the prompt purchase of the ladder truck.

items.title: Personnel Ordinance Amendments
items.summary: Approved moving the Assistant Network Administrator position to a 40-hour work week and authorized a 2.5% wage increase for non-union personnel effective July 1, 2026.

items.title: Proposed Vacant Building Ordinance
items.summary: Approved a new vacant building registration and fee ordinance for first reading to incentivize the occupancy of commercial storefronts. The Council referred the repeal of existing zoning-based vacant property rules to the Community Development Board for further review.

items.title: Medford Square Redevelopment Project Grant
items.summary: Accepted a $450,000 grant from MassDevelopment to fund archaeological excavation and the re-interment of human remains discovered at a former cemetery site. CPA Manager Theresa DuPont noted the site requires due diligence before redevelopment following an incomplete remains removal project in 1959.

items.title: Unfinished Business and Adjournment
items.summary: Placed two old items on file and adjourned following an announcement by Councilor Leming regarding his upcoming six-month military deployment.
